framework.primary_law: India AI Governance Guidelines (voluntary, 5 November 2025) plus IT Rules synthetic media amendment (effective 20 February 2026) and DPDP Act 2023
framework.enforcing_body: Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY); Data Protection Board (once constituted)
framework.max_penalty: IT Rules: loss of safe harbour for intermediaries; DPDP penalties (sources disagree on maximum)
framework.geographic_scope: Intermediaries and data fiduciaries serving users in India.

research.summary: India has no standalone AI law. MeitY issued voluntary AI Governance Guidelines (reported as 5 November 2025) that reject pre-approval of models, with a conversion pathway to mandatory rules reportedly due around November 2026. Binding duties come from the IT Rules amendment on synthetic content (G.S.R. 120(E), effective 20 February 2026: labelling, provenance metadata, three-hour takedown) and the DPDP Act with its November 2025 Rules.

key_provisions.title: Synthetic media labelling
key_provisions.description: Visible labels and machine-readable provenance on synthetic audio and video; three-hour takedown of notified illegal content.

key_provisions.title: DPDP Act 2023
key_provisions.description: Consent, accuracy and purpose limitation for personal data used by AI.

key_provisions.title: AI Governance Guidelines
key_provisions.description: Voluntary principles; no pre-approval of models.

cross_jurisdiction_tensions.tension: India's light-touch stance contrasts with EU obligations; firms serving both must meet the stricter EU rules.

safety_risk_management.rationale: Voluntary guidelines; no mandatory risk assessment.

privacy_data_protection.rationale: DPDP Act provides consent-based protections; board not fully operational.

accountability.rationale: Safe-harbour loss is the main sanction.

access_to_remedy.rationale: Grievance mechanisms exist but are limited.

gaps_and_weaknesses: No omnibus AI law is imminent.
Data Protection Board is not yet fully operating.
Sources disagree on some dates and penalties.
research.monitor_notes: Several dates in the source conflict (guidelines release date; DPDP penalty maximum). Verify against gazette notifications and PIB releases. Scores are provisional AI-drafted judgements against the AIETHOS rubric and reflect protections currently in force.

citizen.one_line: India relies on voluntary guidelines for AI, with firm rules on deepfake labelling and data protection.
citizen.what_changed: Since 20 February 2026, AI-generated audio and video on platforms must be labelled and can be ordered down within three hours if illegal.
citizen.who_is_protected: Users of online platforms and people whose personal data is processed in India.
who_is_not_protected: People affected by AI outside platform and data rules

your_rights.how_to_invoke: Report unlabelled content through the platform grievance process.

your_rights.what_it_means: Consent and correction rights over personal data.
your_rights.how_to_invoke: Raise with the data fiduciary, then the Data Protection Board when operating.

citizen.plain_language_summary: India is leaning on voluntary AI guidance for now, with strict rules on deepfakes and personal data.

jargon_buster.Safe harbour: Legal protection for platforms from liability for user content, lost if they break the rules.
jargon_buster.DPDP: India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act.
